transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Since I started this job and the tech program at the same time, I feel like I’m not handling the pressure well and it’s messing up my school and work. It's just gotten to the point where I feel really overwhelmed trying to balance it all.
Did these symptoms start within a few days of a specific stressful event, or have they been going on for at least several months?

They actually started within a few weeks of when I started the factory job, moved into my new apartment, and began the maintenance program all at once. It hasn't been several months, it's only been going on for about a month now.
Since this started, have you been feeling more sad, anxious, or irritable than usual, or having trouble sleeping or concentrating because of the stress?

I've definitely been feeling really anxious and constantly on edge. It's been really hard to concentrate because I just end up zoning out on my phone and beating myself up instead of focusing on my work. I'm not really sure about my sleep, but the anxiety and lack of focus are definitely major issues for me right now.
Has this stress made it hard for you to keep up with work, school, or relationships in a noticeable way, or caused you to miss responsibilities or perform worse than usual?

Yes, it definitely has. I've already missed several evening classes and had to swap a couple of work shifts at the last minute because of how overwhelmed I've been. Both my academic advisor and my supervisor have warned me that if this keeps up, I could lose my spot in the program and my job.

Did this start after one clear stressful event, or was it mainly because of several life changes happening at the same time? Also, has the stress felt out of proportion to what most people would expect in the same situation?

It was definitely because of multiple major life changes happening all at once, since I started the factory job, began the tech program, and moved into my own apartment in the same month. I do feel like my reaction is out of proportion, because instead of just dealing with the workload, I've ended up shutting down, avoiding classes, and skipping shifts.
Since this started, have you also been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I've completely stopped doing the things I usually enjoy. My usual outlets like basketball, painting, weekend hikes, and my favorite maker meetup have totally fallen by the wayside. Instead, I just feel too overwhelmed and end up sitting in my apartment scrolling on my phone and avoiding everything.
Did this start after a traumatic event involving actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, or was it mainly a reaction to major life stressors like work, school, and moving?

No, there wasn't any kind of traumatic event like that at all. This is entirely a reaction to the major life stressors of starting the new factory job, beginning the tech program, and moving into my own apartment all at the same time.
Have these stress-related symptoms improved at all since they started, or have they stayed the same or gotten worse over the past month?

They haven't really improved; if anything, I've just felt increasingly overwhelmed and stuck in this shut-down state over the past month. I'm holding onto hope that once I get used to the schedule and find a routine, things will ease up and I'll be able to handle it. But right now, I haven't seen any real improvement yet.
Have these symptoms gone away within a few months of the stressors, or have they continued for longer than 6 months after the stressors ended?

They definitely haven't lasted for six months yet, since this has only been going on for about a month and all these stressors are still ongoing. I keep telling myself that once I get used to the schedule and settle into a routine, these overwhelmed feelings should ease up and go away.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life is not worth living since this stress started?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or felt like life isn't worth living. Even though I feel extremely overwhelmed, stressed, and shut down by my current workload, I've never thought about anything like that.
Since this started, have you been feeling mostly sad or hopeless most days, or is it more that you feel stressed and overwhelmed without feeling depressed?

It's definitely more about feeling stressed, overwhelmed, and constantly on edge rather than feeling depressed or hopeless. I feel shut down and avoid my responsibilities because the pressure is just too much, but it's driven by that anxiety and overwhelm rather than deep sadness.

Have any of the main stressors changed or improved at all, or are they still ongoing in the same way? Also, do you think your symptoms would likely get better once the stressors are reduced or you adjust to them?

The stressors are still very much ongoing, since it has only been about a month since everything started at once. I really believe that once I get used to the schedule and the workload settles into a routine, this stressed-out, shut-down feeling will ease up. Once that happens, I think I'll be able to handle things normally again.
